correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all definitions, dimensions and normalization: C=2R-I with R positive; a strict cycle heat-difference Metzler system locates the minimum resolvent diagonal at the center for any rectangle; exact cosine spectrum gives a unique root; reflection images and elliptic lattice Green yield the sharp universal constant; 1D Laplace asymptotics and positive exponential-moment bounds yield parity-sensitive coefficients and all remainder orders. A standalone verifier reconstructs independent rational full matrices and high-precision spectral roots; all 2806 checks passed. Computations support, but do not replace, the analytic infinite claims. The physical timestep factor is twice s.

originality.rationale: The general Cayley/resolvent diagonal criterion is existing work, as are massive square-lattice Green formulas. Compared at the implication level, the substantial full-text Faragó–Horváth 2006 maximum-principle treatment proves a sufficient two-dimensional condition, not the sharp reflecting-rectangle center-minimum theorem nor the parity-specific n^(-1/2) exponential finite-size law. Higueras–Roldán prove sharp but one-dimensional Dirichlet results. Accessible existing records for Neumann compact schemes concern different spatial discretizations or only energy convergence; incomplete full texts leave a documented priority caveat. Dedicated published-finding corpus and prior research records searches did not reveal the complete combined claim. This is qualified self-review originality assessment, not an assertion that searches prove novelty.
residual_risks: The 1992 Kraaijevanger full text was not inspected: it may contain an unrecognized closely related multidimensional threshold.
Sun 2009, Gao–Sun 2012 and Beale 2009 were accessible at abstract level only; uninspected appendices could establish more than the abstracts state.
Classical lattice Green and reflection results could facilitate a previously published equivalent square-grid asymptotic under different terminology.
A self-review is not a specialist independent priority review.

value.rationale: Sharp nonnegative diffusion stepping with no-flux boundaries is a motivated numerical maximum-principle problem. The theorem replaces the classical sufficient physical bound 1/2 by an exact universal bound about 0.58819728; for every finite rectangle it identifies the first failing sites and computes the exact algebraic/trigonometric root. For large squares it gives an unusually informative exponentially small n^(-1/2) correction whose parity coefficient changes by a factor cosh(xi) about 2.70. This is a natural nonroutine structural and asymptotic classification rather than a numerical instance.
